newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa has successful surgery on heart.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa has successful surgery on heart.

text.p: Mother Teresa, the 86-year-old Roman Catholic missionary, underwent a successful X-ray test and surgical procedure to clear a blocked coronary artery on Friday, an Indian heart clinic official said.
"Both the angiography and the angioplasty are over. She is well. It is a success," A.K. Chatterjee, administrator of the B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre in Calcutta, told reporters.
"The angioplasty was done to clear the blockage in her coronary artery," he added.
The procedures were performed eight days after Mother Teresa, a Nobel Peace Prize winner noted for her devotion to the world's poor, entered hospital with an irregular heartbeat.
"I heard that she came out of the operation theatre smiling and doctors congratulated her," Sister Prasanna, a member of Mother Teresa's Missionaries of Charity, told Reuters.
Angiography is an X-ray test which uses an injected opaque dye to show up blocked arteries. Angioplasty is the prodedure to unblock the artery by inserting a balloon and inflating it.
It was the third time Mother Teresa had had coronary angiography and angioplasty. The others were performed in the United States in 1991 and at the Birla centre in 1993.
In a medical bulletin several hours before the procedures, doctors said Mother Teresa's condition had improved and that she had gone 24 hours without chest pains.
Doctors said she had suffered heart failure several times since entering the Woodlands Nursing Home in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta on November 22.
She was moved to the Birla clinic for the angiography on Tuesday. The test was delayed from Wednesday because of her critical health.
On Thursday, they said although Mother Teresa remained in critical condition, her vital signs had stabilised sufficiently to make the test possible.
Chatterjee said at the time that doctors might opt to do both procedures at the same time.
Mother Teresa, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with the poor, was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989.
Throughout her stay in hospital, members of the Missionaries of Charity, which has about 4,500 nuns in some 80 countries and was founded by Mother Teresa in 1949, prayed for her recovery.
